questions.question: What was the first company to use the term "Golden Master"?
Which company's JavaScript engine serves as the foundation that Node.js was built on?
questions.explanation: Node.js was built on Google's V8 JavaScript engine, which was originally developed for the Chrome browser. V8 compiles JavaScript directly to native machine code, giving Node.js its impressive performance for server-side applications.

questions.question: Which popular web framework for the Ruby programming language is known for implementing the MVC pattern?
questions.explanation: Ruby on Rails, often just called "Rails," is a widely used web framework built on the Ruby language that prominently features the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern. MVC separates an application into three components — the model (data), the view (UI), and the controller (logic) — making code easier to manage and scale. Rails helped popularize MVC among web developers when it launched in the mid-2000s.

questions.question: Which classic recursive algorithm is notorious for its exponential time complexity of O(2^n), making it a textbook example of inefficient computation?
questions.explanation: The naive recursive implementation of the Fibonacci sequence recalculates the same subproblems repeatedly, leading to an exponential O(2^n) time complexity. This inefficiency makes it a classic example used in computer science courses to motivate dynamic programming and memoization techniques, which can reduce the complexity to O(n).

questions.question: What book, written by Daniel Friedman and Matthias Felleisen, is credited with guiding Paul Graham in his understanding of the Y Combinator — the concept that later inspired the name of his famous startup accelerator?
questions.explanation: Paul Graham has cited "The Little Schemer" by Daniel Friedman and Matthias Felleisen as a key influence in his deep understanding of the Y Combinator, a fundamental concept in lambda calculus that enables recursion without explicit self-reference. This connection was so meaningful to Graham that he named his influential startup accelerator "Y Combinator" after the concept. The book teaches Scheme, a Lisp dialect, through a distinctive Socratic question-and-answer style.
